name: Naramachi
description: Nara's historic merchant quarter, a warren of narrow lanes lined with preserved townhouses, small museums, craft shops, cafes and traditional restaurants. It is quiet, walkable and full of character, sitting just south of the main sights and offering a calm, authentic base close to the centre.
bestFor: Culture lovers and slow-paced nomads wanting atmosphere near the centre

name: Nara Park Temple Area
description: The leafy heart of Nara around Todai-ji and Kasuga Taisha, where free-roaming deer wander vast parkland dotted with famous temples and shrines. It is scenic and serene, though busy with day visitors, making it more a place to live beside than within.
bestFor: Nature and history fans who want temples and parkland on the doorstep

name: Kintetsu and JR Nara Station Area
description: The practical core of the city around Kintetsu Nara and JR Nara stations, packed with shops, restaurants, cafes and hotels. It offers the best transport links, quick trains to Osaka and Kyoto, and the widest choice of everyday amenities for daily nomad life.
bestFor: Nomads wanting transport links, cafes and everyday convenience nearby
pros: Plenty of cafes to work from
Fast reach to Osaka and Kyoto

name: Nishinokyo
tagline: Quiet temple district west of centre
description: A calm, low-rise district west of the centre near the historic temples of Yakushi-ji and Toshodai-ji. It is residential and peaceful, with a slower pace, cheaper rents and easy rail access, appealing to nomads who prefer quiet over central bustle.
bestFor: Budget-minded nomads wanting calm residential living near notable temples
